brief_rationale: The doctor actively elicited current wound/systemic status, recognized the high-risk diabetic-foot context, gave explicit escalation thresholds, clarified medication and wound-care safety, built a concrete follow-up plan with owner/timing/backup, addressed transport/cost/offloading barriers, and closed with teach-back and no overreach. All eight responsibility-chain items are met without error. Multiple high-order points (HO1–HO4) were triggered and completed with meaningful trajectory impact, including a tiered local/urgent plan, repair of broken antibiotic and vascular follow-up links, bounded closure separating foot/vascular priorities from later chest CT, and discovery of hidden prior amputation and vascular procedure history. No important non-chain defect exists. The trajectory satisfies Strong and exceeds it, meeting Perfect by completing at least two high-order points. Closure is safe, executable, traceable, and valid.

closure_assessment.explanation: The doctor obtained caregiver teach-back on the plan, confirmed red flags, and explicitly limited the assessment to what was known. No fabricated dates, doses, or promises of healing were made. The plan was concrete, with owner, timing, materials, and backup.
